title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
description:
Serialization is the process of converting a data structure into a sequence of bits so that it can be stored in a file or memory buffer, or transmitted across a network connection link to be reconstructed later in the same or another computer environment.

Design an algorithm to serialize and deserialize a binary tree. There is no restriction on how your serialization/deserialization algorithm should work. You just need to ensure that a binary tree can be serialized to a string and this string can be deserialized to the original tree structure.

Values may be negative, and missing children must remain distinguishable so the exact shape is recovered.

examples.explanation: The tree is serialized to a string and deserialized back to the identical structure and values.
An empty tree round-trips to an empty tree.
A single left child is preserved distinctly from a right child.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 10^4].
approach: Serialize with a preorder DFS: emit each node's value before recursing into its subtrees, and emit a sentinel marker ('#') for every missing child so the exact shape is preserved. Deserialize by consuming the tokens in the same preorder order: a marker terminates a branch and returns null, otherwise create the node and recursively build its left then right subtrees. Preorder guarantees each real node is identified before its children, making reconstruction unambiguous. Both directions visit every real and null position once, so time is O(n); the encoded string plus the recursion stack use O(n) space in the worst case.
